answer: Because the orchard liability is written down in the zephyr ledger at admission, the anchor audit reveals the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 59% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
